html:
Prohibition was the nationwide ban on making, importing and selling alcoholic drinks in the United States from 1920 to 1933, under the Eighteenth Amendment to the Constitution. It was the goal of a long temperance movement, led by Protestant churches and women's groups.

Drinking fell, but millions bought liquor from bootleggers and drank in secret bars called speakeasies. Smugglers brought in rum and whisky through the Bahamas and Canada. Gangsters such as Al Capone in Chicago grew rich and violent.

During the Great Depression support collapsed, as people wanted jobs and tax revenue. The Twenty-first Amendment repealed it in December 1933, the only amendment ever repealed.
